Arbiter is a simple publish/subscribe event system for communication between modules. All instances share the same subscribers, so a module can inform others without a reference to them. import Arbiter from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Arbiter'; const onOrderReady = (order) => console.log(order); new Arbiter().subscribe('ORDER/READY', onOrderReady); // Somewhere else new Arbiter().inform('ORDER/READY', { orderId: 12300, total: 100.99, }); Method Description subscribe(event, callback) Calls the callback with the arguments of every inform(). unsubscribe(event, callback) Removes the callback. inform(event, ...args) Calls the subscribers of the event. clearSubscribers(event) Removes all subscribers of the event. getSubscribers(event) Returns the subscribers of the event. An error thrown by a subscriber doesn't stop the others. It's rethrown asynchronously, so it still shows in the console. Combined with ServerJS, the server can inform your modules too: OrderEvents.js import Arbiter from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Arbiter'; export default { ready(order) { new Arbiter().inform('ORDER/READY', order); }, }; $response->bigPipe()->require("require('OrderEvents').ready()", [$order]);

AsyncRequest sends a request to an endpoint that responds with the BigPipe response format. The DOM operations and modules of the response are applied automatically, before your handler is called. import AsyncRequest from 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncRequest'; const request = new AsyncRequest('/ajax/remove.php') .setMethod('POST') .setData({ id: 123 }) .setHandler((response) => { console.log(response.payload); }) .send(); // Cancel the request if it's no longer needed request.abort();

All setters return the request, so they can be chained. Method Description setURI(uri) The URL to call. It can also be passed to the constructor. setMethod(method) The HTTP method, POST by default. setData(data) An object (sent URL-encoded, nested objects as a[b]=c) or a FormData. setRequestHeader(name, value) Adds a request header. setRelative(element) The element that sent the request, see relative targets. send() Sends the request and returns the XMLHttpRequest. abort() Aborts the request. Every request is sent with the X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest header and a __req parameter with a counter of the requests made from the page.

Method Called setInitialHandler(fn) Right before the request is sent. setHandler(fn) With the parsed response, after its DOM operations and modules were applied. setErrorHandler(fn) With the XMLHttpRequest when the status isn't 2xx/3xx or the request failed. setFinallyHandler(fn) With the XMLHttpRequest after the request finished, successfully or not.

Add the token to every request, e.g. in Laravel: const token = document.querySelector('meta[name=csrf-token]').getAttribute('content'); new AsyncRequest('/ajax/save') .setRequestHeader('X-CSRF-TOKEN', token) .send();

Dialog shows modal dialogs with modal-vanilla, which uses the same markup and classes as Bootstrap modals. Dialogs can be stacked: each new one is shown above the previous one and Esc closes only the topmost. The server usually opens dialogs with DialogResponse, see Dialogs API. You can also open them from JavaScript.

Builds the dialog from a title, body and footer: import Dialog from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Dialog'; new Dialog().showFromModel({ title: 'Dialog title', body: 'html content', footer: '', controller: 'ModalLogger', backdrop: 'static', });

Shows a dialog from your own markup, the content of .modal: new Dialog().render({ content: `
...
`, dialogClassName: 'modal-lg', });

Option Default Description controller A module name or a function called with the dialog, see below. backdrop true false for no backdrop, 'static' for one that doesn't close it. keyboard true Close the dialog with Esc. animate false Animate showing and hiding. transition 0 Duration of the dialog transition in ms. backdropTransition 0 Duration of the backdrop transition in ms. timeout Show the dialog after this many ms. The method then returns a Promise.

A controller is called with the modal and the arguments passed to the method. Use it to react to the events of the dialog: show, shown, hide, hidden and dismiss. ModalLogger.js export default class ModalLogger { constructor(modal, ...args) { modal.on('shown', () => console.log('shown', args)); modal.on('hidden', () => console.log('hidden')); } }
const dialog = new Dialog(); dialog.closeCurrent(); // the topmost dialog dialog.close(2); // the last two dialogs dialog.close(); // all dialogs
The helpers that the DOM operations are built on. Use them to change the page from your own modules the same way the server does.

import DOM from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/DOM'; const list = document.querySelector('ul.logs'); DOM.appendContent(list, '
  • appended line
    • '); Method Description setContent(node, html) Replaces the content of the node. appendContent(node, html) Inserts HTML as the last child. prependContent(node, html) Inserts HTML as the first child. insertAfter(node, html) Inserts HTML after the node. insertBefore(node, html) Inserts HTML before the node. replace(node, html) Replaces the node with HTML. remove(node) Removes the node. empty(node) Removes all children of the node. caution The HTML is inserted as is. Escape any user input on the server.

Find the closest ancestor of a node, including the node itself: import { byTag, byClass, byAttribute, find } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Parent'; byTag(event.target, 'a'); byClass(event.target, 'card'); byAttribute(event.target, 'data-id'); find(event.target, (node) => node.dataset?.id === '123');
A shortcut for document.getElementById(): import $ from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/$'; $('chart').classList.add('ready');

bigpipe-util is the JavaScript runtime of BigPipe. It sends requests, applies the DOM operations the server responds with and calls the JavaScript modules the server asks for. The server side is usually bigpipe-php, but any backend that speaks the response format works.

A bundler, such as webpack or Vite. bigpipe-util ships both ES modules and CommonJS and doesn't depend on a specific bundler. Loading your own modules by name is up to your application, see step 2. A backend that answers with BigPipe responses, e.g. richarddobron/bigpipe for PHP 8.0+.
npm install bigpipe-util

In your entrypoint (e.g. resources/js/app.js), start the Primer and tell BigPipe how to load your modules. The server refers to them by name, e.g. require('UserLoggedInAlert'), and BigPipe calls the loader to get the module. The loader has to return the module itself (its default export) synchronously. webpack resources/js/app.js import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; import { setModuleLoader } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry'; Primer(); setModuleLoader(modulePath => require('./' + modulePath).default); Vite resources/js/app.js import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; import { setModuleLoader } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/ModuleRegistry'; Primer(); // Eager, because modules are called synchronously. The entrypoint itself is excluded. const modules = import.meta.glob(['./**/*.js', '!./app.js'], { eager: true }); setModuleLoader(modulePath => modules[`./${modulePath}.js`]?.default); Any name is loaded relative to the entrypoint, so require('UserLoggedInAlert') on the server loads resources/js/UserLoggedInAlert.js. Names can contain folders, e.g. Admin/Panel. A loader that returns nothing for a name makes BigPipe throw module "..." was not found. Modules of this package are resolved automatically. The server may refer to them as bigpipe-util/src/... (or bigpipe-util/dist/...); you don't need to handle them in the loader. setModuleLoader() also defines window.require, which the inline script in the next step uses. Pass { global: false } as the second argument to prevent it. Single modules can be registered under an exact name with registerModules({ Name: module }). They win over the loader.

Dialogs use modal-vanilla, which imports the Node.js module events. Vite doesn't polyfill Node.js modules for the browser, so loading fails with Class extends value [object Object] is not a constructor or null. Install the npm package of the same name and point the import to it (the trailing slash selects the package instead of the Node.js module): npm install events vite.config.js export default defineConfig({ resolve: { alias: { events: 'events/' } } }); Restart Vite with --force to rebuild its dependency cache. webpack 5 picks the events package up on its own when it's installed.

Defining window.require yourself still works when no loader is set, so existing setups don't have to change. The loader above replaces the bigpipe-util/ branch of the old function: you only write the part for your own modules.

At the end of the page, pass the modules required during the page render to ServerJS. Wait for DOMContentLoaded: layout.php <script> document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/ServerJS"))).handle(<?=json_encode(\dobron\BigPipe\BigPipe::jsmods())?>); }); </script> Vite adds your entrypoint as <script type="module">, and module scripts are deferred: they run after the HTML is parsed, so an inline script at the end of the page would run before window.require exists. Module scripts run before DOMContentLoaded, so this works with every bundler.

documents.t: Some warnings (e.g. a DOM operation that matches nothing) are logged only when __DEV__ is defined and truthy. In webpack define it with DefinePlugin, in Vite with define: vite.config.js export default defineConfig({ define: { __DEV__: JSON.stringify(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production') } });

A module is a default export: a function, a class or an object. resources/js/MyModule.js export default class MyModule { init(...args) { console.log('Hello world!', args); } } Call it from the server: $response = new \dobron\BigPipe\AsyncResponse(); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('MyModule').init()", [ 'first argument', 'second argument', ]); $response->send();
Make links and forms asynchronous with the Primer. Send requests from your code with AsyncRequest. Learn what the server sends back in How it works.

BigPipe moves the decision about what happens on the page to the server. The browser only sends a request, the server answers with a list of instructions and bigpipe-util executes them. The user clicks a link or submits a form handled by the Primer, or your code sends an AsyncRequest. The server responds with DOM operations (domops) and JavaScript modules to call (jsmods). AsyncResponse applies the DOM operations, then ServerJS loads and calls the modules.

A response is JSON prefixed with the for (;;); shield. The shield makes the response unusable when it's loaded with a <script> tag from another site; AsyncRequest strips it before parsing. for (;;);{"payload":null,"domops":[...],"jsmods":{"require":[...]},"__ar":1} Key Description payload Custom data for your handler, see setPayload() on the server. domops DOM operations, applied in order. jsmods Modules to call, see ServerJS. __ar Marks the response as an async response. The whole response object is also passed to the handler set with setHandler().

Each operation is an array [type, selector, targetRelative, content]: ["appendContent", "ul.logs", false, {"__html": "
  • appended line
    • "}] type: one of setContent, appendContent, prependContent, insertAfter, insertBefore, replace, remove, hide, show and eval. selector: a CSS selector of the element to change. targetRelative: when true, the operation targets the element that sent the request (the clicked link or the submitted form), or the element matching selector inside it. The PHP library sets it when the selector is empty. content: HTML wrapped in the __html transport marker, or JavaScript code for eval, which runs with this bound to the element. Operations whose selector matches nothing are skipped. With __DEV__ defined and truthy (see Getting started), an error is logged to the console.

AsyncRequest hands every successful response to AsyncResponse. You can use it directly to process a response you received in another way, e.g. over a WebSocket: import AsyncResponse from 'bigpipe-util/dist/async/AsyncResponse'; socket.addEventListener('message', ({ data }) => { new AsyncResponse().handle(JSON.parse(data)); });

A pagelet is an independent part of the page, like a sidebar or a feed, with its own content, CSS and JavaScript. BigPipe shows each pagelet as soon as its CSS is loaded and runs the JavaScript of the pagelets only after all of them are displayed, so scripts never delay the content. The server renders the pagelets, see dobron\BigPipe\Pagelet in the PHP library. For every pagelet, it outputs: (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/BigPipe"))).onPageletArrive({ id: "sidebar", css: ["/css/sidebar.css"], js: ["/js/sidebar.js"], domops: [["setContent", "#sidebar", false, {"__html": "..."}]], jsmods: {"require": [["Sidebar", "init", []]]}, is_last: true, }); Like the inline script of ServerJS, it needs require to exist. When the entrypoint is loaded as <script type="module"> (Vite), it runs after the page is parsed. Use <script type="module"> for the inline scripts as well: they run in document order after the entrypoint, and the pagelets are displayed once the page has been parsed instead of while it streams. With a classic <script src> (webpack) the entrypoint, placed before the pagelets, makes them display progressively.

Arrive. The CSS files of the pagelet start loading. Files shared by more pagelets are loaded once. Display. When its CSS is loaded, the DOM operations of the pagelet are applied. Load JS. When the last pagelet (is_last) has arrived and all pagelets are displayed, the JS files of all pagelets start loading. Run. When the JS files of a pagelet are loaded, its jsmods are handled by ServerJS. The phases are exported as BIGPIPE_PHASE, PAGELET_PHASE and RESOURCE_PHASE from bigpipe-util/dist/BigPipe. BigPipe is a singleton, so new BigPipe() always returns the same instance with the registered pagelets.

The Primer makes links and forms asynchronous without writing any JavaScript. It registers a single click and submit listener on the document, so it also works for content added later. import Primer from 'bigpipe-util/dist/Primer'; Primer();

Add the URL to call in ajaxify and pick the behaviour with rel: Remove item rel Method Description async GET Sends the request and handles the response. async-post POST The same as async, but with POST. dialog POST Intended for requests that open a dialog. Links with a real href (other than #) still open normally when clicked with the middle mouse button or with a modifier key, so users can open them in a new tab.

Forms with rel="async" are submitted in the background. The form data, including the name and value of the button that submitted it, is sent to ajaxify or, if missing, to action, with the form's method. <form action="/ajax/subscribe.php" method="POST" rel="async"> <input name="email" type="email"> <button type="submit" name="plan" value="free">Subscribe</button> </form> While the request is running: the inputs, selects and textareas are made read-only and the submit button is disabled, unless the form has the disable-prevent-form class, an element with the form-loader class inside the form gets the loading class.

The link or form gets the async-saving class while its request is running. Clicks on a link with this class are ignored, which prevents double submits. Use it to show a spinner: .async-saving { cursor: progress; opacity: 0.6; }
The link or form becomes the relative element of the request. DOM operations with an empty selector target it, see DOM operations.

ServerJS calls the JavaScript modules that the server requires. It handles the jsmods of every response and, at the end of the page, the modules required while rendering it: <script> document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { (new (require("bigpipe-util/src/ServerJS"))).handle(<?=json_encode(\dobron\BigPipe\BigPipe::jsmods())?>); }); </script>

jsmods.require is a list of [module, method, args]: { "require": [ ["UserLoggedInAlert", null, ["Marvin"]], ["ChartRenderer", "render", [{"__e": "chart"}, [10, 20, 30]]] ] } The module is resolved by the loader set with setModuleLoader(), see Getting started. Without a method, the module is called as a constructor with the arguments: new UserLoggedInAlert('Marvin'). An instance is only created, if it was not yet. With a method, a class is instantiated without arguments and the method is called with them: new ChartRenderer().render(element, [10, 20, 30]). A module that exports an object has the method called on the object directly. In PHP: $response->bigPipe()->require("require('UserLoggedInAlert')", ['Marvin']); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('ChartRenderer').render()", [ \dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker::transportElement('chart'), [10, 20, 30], ]);

A call with a method creates a new object of a class every time. To keep one object and talk to it from more calls, the server defines an instance in jsmods.instances, a list of [id, module, args]: { "instances": [["__inst_u_0_1", "ChartRenderer", [{"__e": "chart"}, [10, 20, 30]]]], "require": [ ["__inst_u_0_1", "render"], ["Dashboard", "add", [{"__m": "__inst_u_0_1"}]] ] } The instance is created with new ChartRenderer(element, [10, 20, 30]) the first time something requires it, by its id in require or in a __m transport marker, and every later use gets the same object, also in the following responses. In PHP: $chart = $response->bigPipe()->instance('ChartRenderer', [ \dobron\BigPipe\TransportMarker::transportElement('chart'), [10, 20, 30], ]); $chart->call('render'); $response->bigPipe()->require("require('Dashboard').add()", [$chart]);

Arguments are JSON, so values that JSON can't express are sent as markers and replaced before the module is called: Marker Replaced with PHP __e The element with this id. TransportMarker::transportElement() __m The module, resolved the same way as require. TransportMarker::transportModule() __map A Map created from the list of [key, value]. TransportMarker::transportMap() __set A Set created from the list of values. TransportMarker::transportSet() __html Used for the HTML content of DOM operations. TransportMarker::transportHtml() Markers are replaced at any depth of the arguments.

Calls the callback after the load event of the window, or on the next tick if the page is already loaded. import onAfterLoad from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/onAfterLoad'; onAfterLoad(() => console.log('The page is loaded.'));

Clicks made before the page is loaded would be lost, because the handlers aren't attached yet. waitForLoad defers them: it shows the progress cursor, waits for the page to load and then calls the callback. Then it follows the href of a link, or repeats the click when the callback returns false or the element isn't a link, so the click is handled by the listeners attached in the meantime. import { byTag } from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/Parent'; import onAfterLoad from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/onAfterLoad'; import waitForLoad from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/waitForLoad'; const clickHandler = (event) => { const link = byTag(event.target, 'A'); if (!link || !/async(?:-post)?|dialog/.test(link.rel)) { return; } event.preventDefault(); waitForLoad(link, event, () => false); }; document.documentElement.addEventListener('click', clickHandler); onAfterLoad(() => { document.documentElement.removeEventListener('click', clickHandler); }); Put this code inline in the <head>, so it runs before the rest of your JavaScript is loaded.
import ReloadPage from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ReloadPage'; new ReloadPage().now(); new ReloadPage().delay(250); // in ms The server calls it with $response->reload($delay).
import ServerRedirect from 'bigpipe-util/dist/core/ServerRedirect'; new ServerRedirect().redirectPageTo('/onboarding', 500); // delay in ms The server calls it with $response->redirect($url, $delay).
